We have applied first template 324324, got product(s) as precursors: It returned a tuple of two SMILES: ('Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1', 'Nc1ccccc1N'). That suggests the retrosynthetic step splits the amide? Actually original target had ...C(=O)N c3ccccc3N (an anilide with an aniline). The template likely breaks the amide to give carboxylic acid and aniline? The result shows product 1: same as target but with C(=O)O (carboxylic acid) instead of C(=O)N... and product 2: Nc1ccccc1N (para-diaminobenzene? Actually it's an aniline with NH2 at both ends? Wait Nc1ccccc1N is aniline with two NH? That's p-phenylenediamine? Actually SMILES: N c1 c c c c c1 N => aniline with two NH groups at both ends? That's p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene). So step 1 yields acid and diamine.

Now we need to apply second template 1914396 to the acid product? Let's check. Apply to the acid SMILES.
